content.text: When a team is asked to rethink a familiar process, the first response is often to {{gap:1}} the proposal aside, particularly when previous reforms have increased paperwork without improving the result. A skilled facilitator will {{gap:2}} account of existing concerns, {{gap:3}} on the team's experience and {{gap:4}} sight of the pressures of the working day. Rather than treating resistance as proof that people dislike change, the facilitator asks which part of the proposal creates a practical obstacle and which part merely challenges a habit. This approach can {{gap:5}} about useful changes without {{gap:6}} credibility to the people who must put them into practice. It also helps the group {{gap:7}} a distinction between genuine risks and objections that can be {{gap:8}} out once the evidence has been considered. The final recommendation is consequently more persuasive because it acknowledges inconvenience instead of hiding it behind enthusiastic language.

questions.explanation: Set aside means postpone or reserve for later consideration.

distractorExplanations.B: Put aside is possible in other contexts, but set aside is the more precise fixed expression here.
distractorExplanations.C: Lay aside is formal and uncommon in this modern workplace context.
distractorExplanations.D: Cast aside usually means reject or discard, which is stronger than the intended meaning.

questions.explanation: Take account of is the established expression.

distractorExplanations.A: Give account of means explain or report, not consider.
distractorExplanations.C: Hold account of is not idiomatic.
distractorExplanations.D: Make account of is not the standard expression.

questions.explanation: Draw on experience means use it as a resource.

distractorExplanations.B: Pull on experience is not idiomatic.
distractorExplanations.C: Bring on experience changes the meaning and does not fit the preposition.
distractorExplanations.D: Reach on experience is not grammatical.

questions.explanation: Keep sight of is the fixed expression meaning remain aware of something.

distractorExplanations.B: Lose sight of means stop being aware of something.
distractorExplanations.C: Make sight of is not idiomatic.
distractorExplanations.D: Set sight of is not the standard expression.

questions.explanation: Bring about means cause something to happen.

distractorExplanations.C: Take about does not mean cause in this structure.
distractorExplanations.D: Turn about would suggest reversal or movement, not causation.

questions.explanation: Lend credibility to means make something seem trustworthy.

distractorExplanations.A: Lose credibility means become less trusted, the opposite of the intended meaning.
distractorExplanations.B: Give credibility is possible but does not form the intended collocation here.

questions.explanation: Make a distinction means recognise a meaningful difference.

distractorExplanations.B: Do a distinction is not idiomatic.
distractorExplanations.C: Draw a distinction is possible, but make is the intended neutral collocation.
distractorExplanations.D: Set a distinction is not the standard expression.

questions.explanation: Rule out means decide that something is not possible or suitable.

distractorExplanations.A: Take out has several meanings but does not fit the idea of excluding an objection.
distractorExplanations.C: Hold out means resist or remain available, not exclude.
distractorExplanations.D: Cut out does not fit the formal decision-making context.
